summary: POC scoping focused on unit economics for a Celestia Health pilot. Discussed target throughput, average request/response token counts, latency SLOs, privacy constraints (PHI), and benchmark plan. Main topics: per-token estimates, batching and KV/prefix caching knobs, hosted vs dedicated tradeoffs, budget caps for pilot, and security requirements. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send cost spreadsheet and benchmark plan; Celestia to provide sample traces and security contacts.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros, then we'll dive into the POC scope and cost model.
[00:12] Maya Singh: Hi, Maya here. we'll be leading ML side for Celestia, thanks.
[00:18] Robert Lane: Robert, CTO. main focus is cost predictability and PHI handling.
[00:23] Alex Chen: Great. Priya from our side will cover technical knobs. Priya?
[00:28] Priya Patel: Hey all, thanks. quick agenda: we want to understand your traffic shape (qps, burstiness), avg prompt + response tokens, target latency SLO, and budget for the pilot. then propose a benchmark that measures throughput/cost/quality trade-offs.
[00:42] Elena Garcia: For Ops: budget is the big one. we have a 3-month pilot cap of about $12k, prefer hosted but can consider dedicated if it makes sense.
[00:52] Samir Patel: Also need to confirm we never log PHI to third-party systems. encryption/KMS and VPC requirements likely.
[01:00] Priya Patel: Understood. we have private deployment options plus VPC peering and customer-managed KMS for Private. for hosted API, we offer agreement-backed data controls and optional enterprise data routing. (slight overlap)
[01:15] Maya Singh: On workload: our average prompt is ~180 tokens, average response 240 tokens, peak qps is about 8, steady around 2-3. most requests are short clinical summarizations.
[01:30] Priya Patel: OK that helps. so rough per-interaction tokens ~420. we do per-token pricing modeling but the real lever is batching and prefix/KV cache reuse if you have repeated prompts. are your prompts highly templated?
[01:42] Maya Singh: yes, templated templates — e.g., clinician note + patient summary. many prefixes repeat.
[01:50] Priya Patel: perfect — KV cache and prefix caching can massively reduce token compute for repeated context. also batching helps during bursts to amortize per-token overheads.
[01:58] Robert Lane: Can you give numbers? like cost per call with and without caching? ballpark is fine.
[02:05] Alex Chen: quick ballpark: on Redwood hosted with an open-ish model, raw per-token infra cost could be in the low microcents range; with batching and KV reuse you might see effective cost per call drop by 40-70% depending on cache hit rate. for a 420 token call, naive cost might be X, with caching it's so much lower — we'll send a spreadsheet. (note: speaker said 'micro-sents' instead of microcents)
[02:30] Priya Patel: Also model choice matters — smaller quantized variants can cut costs considerably with small quality trade-offs. we can run side-by-side benchmarks: base model, quantized 4-bit, and a variant optimized for latency.
[02:44] Elena Garcia: If we do dedicated, what's the break-even vs hosted? we don't want to overcommit.
[02:50] Priya Patel: Break-even depends on sustained throughput. with steady 8 QPS you'd likely not hit dedicated break-even in a small pilot. dedicated shines for high sustained throughput and predictable latency. for pilot, hosted with reserved burst limits is usually recommended.
[03:05] Samir Patel: Security: SOC2, SAML/SSO, audit logs — what do you provide?
[03:10] Alex Chen: we have SOC2 Type II, support SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and can integrate with customer KMS for private deployments. we'll include the security pack and contact for SOC2.
[03:20] Maya Singh: On benchmarks: we'd like to see latency p50/p95, token cost, quality regression metrics on our eval set and throughput under load. can you run an on-prem-like run?
[03:32] Priya Patel: yes — plan is a two-part benchmark: 1) single node latency & quality, 2) scaled throughput test with controlled concurrency and batching. for on-prem-like we can use our Private deployment env or run a dedicated-like config in hosted with reserved GPUs. we'll propose timelines.
[03:46] Robert Lane: Timeline expectations? pilot start to finish?
[03:50] Alex Chen: Typical: sign-off + security checklist (1 week), ingest sample traces + setup (1 week), benchmark run (1 week), analysis & decision (1 week) — so roughly 4 weeks from go-ahead. we can compress if needed.
[04:06] Elena Garcia: Need clear cost cap — $12k for pilot. can you show expected burn across model variants?
[04:12] Priya Patel: We'll map expected per-token costs and project burn assuming your traffic profile and cache hit rates. we'll include sensitivity for batching sizes and cache hit %.
[04:22] Maya Singh: A concrete ask: can you show scenario A: no cache, small batch; B: 50% cache hit, medium batching; C: 80% cache hit, large batching.
[04:32] Priya Patel: Absolutely. we'll run the triage and return a spreadsheet.
[04:36] Alex Chen: a note on measurement noise — quality regressions are subtle. we'll tie automated evals to your prompts and manual spot checks.
[04:45] Samir Patel: who runs the benchmark and where are logs stored? we need assurance no PHI leaves the VPC if private run.
[04:52] Priya Patel: for private runs we can run inside your VPC or in our Private deployment with customer-managed KMS; logs can be stored in your S3 behind your controls. for hosted runs we'll pseudonymize inputs and can run with enterprise-only agreements.
[05:05] Robert Lane: great. small nit: last time we saw "Redwood Dedicate" in a deck; is that the same as Dedicated? just making sure naming is consistent.
[05:12] Alex Chen: yeah, some decks have typos. Dedicated is the reserved capacity product; Redwood Dedicated. we'll be consistent in the spreadsheet.
[05:18] Maya Singh: OK next steps recap?
[05:20] Alex Chen: recap: Alex sends per-token cost workbook, Priya sends benchmark plan and proposed schedule, Celestia shares traces and success criteria, Robert shares SOC2 contact. follow-up in ~10 days.
[05:32] Elena Garcia: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[05:35] Alex Chen: thanks, we'll follow up by Friday with the artifacts. bye.
